question: Where was Lencho's house located? 🏠
options: In the middle of a dense forest 🌲
On the crest of a low hill ⛰️
At the bottom of a deep valley 🏞️
In the center of a busy town 🏙️
answer: On the crest of a low hill ⛰️
explanation: Brilliant! Lencho's house was the only one in the entire valley, sitting peacefully on the crest (top) of a low hill overlooking his fields. 🌄
hint: It was at a height from where he could see the river and his cornfield.

question: What did the earth desperately need before the harvest? 🌱
explanation: Excellent! The only thing the dry earth needed for a good harvest was a good rain or at least a gentle shower. 💧
hint: Lencho kept looking at the sky hoping for this.

question: What did Lencho compare the large raindrops to? 💧
explanation: Perfect! Lencho was so happy about the rain that he called the large drops ten cent pieces and the little ones fives, because they meant money from a good harvest. 🌾
hint: He gave them a monetary value based on their size.

question: What did the hailstones resemble when they started falling? 🧊
explanation: Awesome! The author ironically compares the destructive hailstones to 'new silver coins' and later the boys treat them like 'frozen pearls'. 🌨️
hint: It is a shiny, valuable metal.

question: What completely destroyed Lencho's cornfield just when he was expecting a good harvest? 🌽
explanation: Fantastic! Lencho was hoping for a gentle rain, but the weather quickly turned into a devastating hailstorm that left his field completely white and ruined. 🌧️
hint: It looked as if the field was covered in salt.

question: How did the field look after the hailstorm had passed? 🌨️
options: It was white, as if covered with salt 🧂
answer: It was white, as if covered with salt 🧂
explanation: Spot on! The hailstones covered the entire field, making it look stark white, as though someone had poured salt all over it. 🏔️
hint: Think of a white seasoning used in everyday cooking.

question: Who did Lencho have unwavering faith in? 🙏
explanation: Great job! Lencho's single hope after the destruction of his crops was the help of God, whose eyes see everything. ✨
hint: He wrote a letter to this supreme being.

question: How much money did Lencho ask for in his letter? ✉️
explanation: Wonderful! He calculated that he needed exactly 100 pesos to sow his field again and to live until the next crop came. 🌽
hint: It is a three-digit number representing a century.

question: Who first read Lencho's letter to God? 📩
explanation: Superb! A postman, who was also an employee at the post office, found the letter in the mailbox and brought it to his boss, laughing heartily. 😂
hint: This person collected the mail from the drop box.

question: How did the postmaster initially react to the letter? 😂
explanation: Outstanding! The postmaster, a fat and amiable fellow, initially broke out laughing at the unusual address before turning serious. 😐
hint: He found the idea of a letter addressed to God very funny at first.

question: Why did the postmaster decide to answer the letter? 🖋️
options: He wanted to play a prank 🃏
He felt bad for Lencho's family 👨‍👩‍👦
In order not to shake the writer's faith in God 🕊️
He was ordered by the government 🏛️
answer: In order not to shake the writer's faith in God 🕊️
explanation: Marvelous! Deeply moved by Lencho's unwavering faith, the postmaster decided to collect money and reply to preserve that pure belief. 🌟
hint: He wished he had the same faith as the man who wrote the letter.

question: How much money was the postmaster able to collect? 💰
explanation: Terrific! Despite asking for help from his employees and friends, he could only collect 70 pesos, which was more than half of what Lencho asked for. 💵
hint: Lencho later complains that he is missing 30 pesos.

question: What was the only word written as a signature on the letter sent to Lencho? ✍️
explanation: Good work! To keep the illusion and preserve Lencho's faith, the postmaster signed the letter with just one word: God. ✨
hint: It was the same name to whom the letter was addressed.

question: How did Lencho react when he saw the money in the envelope? 💵
options: He showed not the slightest surprise 😐
answer: He showed not the slightest surprise 😐
explanation: Splendid! Lencho's faith was so strong and confident that he wasn't surprised at all to receive money from God. 🕊️
hint: His reaction was very calm because he fully expected it.

question: Why did Lencho become angry when he counted the money? 😡
explanation: Phenomenal! Lencho asked for 100 pesos but found only 70. He believed God couldn't make a mistake, so he felt cheated. 😠
hint: It was less than the 100 pesos he asked for.

question: What did Lencho ask God to do in his second letter? ✉️
options: To send the rest of the money, but not through the mail 📬
To give him a new house 🏠
answer: To send the rest of the money, but not through the mail 📬
explanation: Brilliant! He asked for the remaining 30 pesos, but specifically requested God not to send it through the mail because he mistrusted the post office staff. 📮
hint: He wanted the money sent directly because he suspected the postal workers.

question: What did Lencho call the post office employees in his second letter? 🕵️
explanation: Perfect! In a classic twist of irony, Lencho calls the very people who helped him 'a bunch of crooks', thinking they stole his 30 pesos. 🎭
hint: It's a phrase that means a group of thieves or dishonest people.

question: What literary device is heavily used in the ending of 'A Letter to God'? 🎭
explanation: Awesome! Situational irony is present because the post office employees who sacrificed to help Lencho end up being accused of stealing by him. 🤦
hint: It occurs when the outcome is the exact opposite of what is expected.

question: How is Lencho described in the story? 🧑‍🌾
explanation: Excellent! The author describes Lencho as an 'ox of a man', working like an animal in the fields, but still knowing how to write. 💪
hint: He is compared to a strong, hard-working farm animal.

question: What does the word 'pesos' refer to in the story? 💵
options: Currency of several Latin American countries 🪙
answer: Currency of several Latin American countries 🪙
explanation: Spot on! A peso is the basic monetary unit used in several Latin American countries, indicating the story's geographical setting. 🌍
hint: It is the money Lencho asked for.

question: What were the older boys doing before it started raining? 👦
explanation: Great job! The older boys were working hard in the field while the smaller ones were playing near the house until dinner was ready. 🍽️
hint: They were helping their father with the farming.

question: How did Lencho's wife reply when he said they were going to get some water? 👩
explanation: Wonderful! His wife, who was preparing supper, replied 'Yes, God willing,' showing a deep, everyday faith in God's providence. 🍲
hint: She expressed that it depends on the Almighty's wish.

question: For how long did the hail rain on the valley? ⏳
explanation: Superb! The hail rained for an hour on the house, the garden, the hillside, the cornfield, and the whole valley. ❄️
hint: It equals 60 minutes.

question: What was Lencho's only hope left in his heart? ❤️
explanation: Outstanding! Despite the total loss of his crops, Lencho’s heart was filled with one solitary hope: help from God. 🕊️
hint: He believed no one dies of hunger because of this divine entity.

question: What did the postmaster do to collect the money? 💸
options: He gave part of his salary and asked friends for charity 🤝
He asked the government for funds 🏛️
answer: He gave part of his salary and asked friends for charity 🤝
explanation: Marvelous! The postmaster gave part of his own salary and convinced his employees and friends to give something 'for an act of charity'. ❤️
hint: He used his own money and contributions from colleagues.

question: What did Lencho do immediately after counting the money? 😡
options: He went to the window to ask for paper and ink 📝
answer: He went to the window to ask for paper and ink 📝
explanation: Terrific! Angry about the missing 30 pesos, he immediately went to the post office window to get paper and ink to write his second letter. 🖋️
hint: He wanted to write a complaint right away.

question: Who is the poet of the poem 'Dust of Snow'? ✍️
explanation: Good work! 'Dust of Snow' is a beautiful, concise poem written by the famous American poet Robert Frost. 🌨️
hint: His last name relates to cold weather.

question: In 'Dust of Snow', what falls on the poet? ❄️
explanation: Splendid! A crow shakes a hemlock tree, causing fine particles of snow (dust of snow) to fall on the poet. ☃️
hint: It is mentioned in the title of the poem.

question: What tree is mentioned in the poem 'Dust of Snow'? 🌲
explanation: Phenomenal! The poet sits under a Hemlock tree, which is a poisonous plant with small white flowers, traditionally symbolizing sorrow. ☠️
hint: It is known as a poisonous tree.

question: What does the crow usually symbolize in literature? 🐦‍⬛
explanation: Brilliant! Usually, a crow represents gloom, doom, and bad omens. Frost deliberately uses it to show that even 'negative' things can bring positive change. 🖤
hint: It is often associated with darkness and negativity.

question: How does the dust of snow affect the poet's mood? 😌
options: It changes his mood for the better 🌟
answer: It changes his mood for the better 🌟
explanation: Excellent! The sudden, simple act of nature falling on him shakes off his sad thoughts and lifts his spirits completely. ✨
hint: It 'saved some part of a day'.

question: What does the poet mean by 'saved some part of a day I had rued'? ⏳
options: He saved his money that day 💵
He prevented his day from being completely wasted in regret 😌
answer: He prevented his day from being completely wasted in regret 😌
explanation: Perfect! 'Rued' means held in regret. The snow shower brought joy to his heart, saving the rest of his day from being ruined by sadness. ❤️
hint: He stopped regretting and started feeling better.

question: What is the rhyme scheme of 'Dust of Snow'? 🎶
explanation: Awesome! The poem follows an 'abab cdcd' pattern (crow/snow, me/tree, heart/part, mood/rued), making it rhythmic and musical. 🎹
hint: Look at the ending sounds: crow-snow (a), me-tree (b).

question: What underlying theme does Robert Frost convey in 'Dust of Snow'? 🌿
options: Even seemingly negative things in nature can heal the human soul 🌱
answer: Even seemingly negative things in nature can heal the human soul 🌱
explanation: Fantastic! Frost uses 'negative' symbols (crow, hemlock) to show that nature, in any form, has the power to uplift a person's mood. 💚
hint: It shows a positive twist to conventionally negative symbols.

question: Who is the poet of 'Fire and Ice'? ✍️
explanation: Spot on! Robert Frost wrote 'Fire and Ice', using the contrasting elements to discuss the end of the world and human emotions. 🔥
hint: He is the same poet who wrote 'Dust of Snow'.

question: In the poem, what does 'Fire' symbolize? 🔥
explanation: Great job! Frost uses 'Fire' as a metaphor for deep human desires, unending greed, and passionate longing that can destroy humanity. 💥
hint: It represents intense, burning human wants.

question: In the poem, what does 'Ice' symbolize? 🧊
explanation: Wonderful! 'Ice' stands for cold reasoning, hatred, and indifference towards others, which is equally capable of destroying the world. ❄️
hint: It is associated with a lack of warmth and empathy.

question: What are the two views discussed in 'Fire and Ice' regarding the end of the world? 🌍
explanation: Superb! The poem explores two popular theories: the world ending in fiery destruction (desire) or a freezing ice age (hatred). 🌐
hint: They are the two elements mentioned in the title.

question: Which view does the poet agree with first? 🥇
options: He thinks the world won't end 🌍
explanation: Outstanding! The poet states, 'From what I’ve tasted of desire / I hold with those who favor fire', showing his initial agreement with the fire theory. ❤️‍🔥
hint: He associates it with what he has 'tasted of desire'.

question: What does the poet say is 'also great' for destruction? 💥
explanation: Marvelous! He notes that if the world had to perish twice, the cold, calculating nature of Ice (hatred) is also great for destruction. ❄️
hint: It is the second element in the poem's title.

question: What does the word 'perish' mean in the context of the poem? ☠️
explanation: Terrific! 'Perish' means to suffer complete ruin or destruction, referring here to the end of the world. 🌑
hint: It is a synonym for die or decay.

question: What does the poet mean by 'if it had to perish twice'? 🔄
options: If the world gets a second chance 🌱
If the world had to be destroyed a second time 💥
If fire didn't work the first time 🧯
answer: If the world had to be destroyed a second time 💥
explanation: Good work! Frost is saying that if the world were to end a second time, hatred (ice) would be more than sufficient to do the job. 🕰️
hint: It refers to the world ending again.

question: What literary device is used in the line 'I hold with those who favor fire'? ✍️
explanation: Splendid! The repetition of the 'f' sound in 'favor fire' is a classic example of alliteration, adding a musical quality to the poem. 🎵
hint: Notice the repetition of the starting 'f' sound.

question: How are Fire and Ice similar in the poem? ⚖️
options: They both result in the destruction of the world 💥
They are both made of water 💧
answer: They both result in the destruction of the world 💥
explanation: Phenomenal! Though they represent opposite human emotions (desire vs. hatred), they are equally destructive and lethal to humanity. 🥀
hint: Think about their ultimate effect on the world.

question: What is the rhyme scheme of 'Fire and Ice'? 🎶
explanation: Brilliant! The rhyme scheme is aba (fire/desire/fire), abc (twice/hate/ice), bcb (ice/great/suffice), linking the elements together musically. 🎹
hint: Look at the ends of the lines: fire, ice, desire, fire.

question: According to the poet, what 'suffice' means? ✅
explanation: Excellent! The word 'suffice' means to be enough or adequate. Ice (hatred) would be enough to destroy the world. 📏
hint: It shares a root with the word 'sufficient'.

question: What is the central message of Robert Frost's 'Fire and Ice'? 🌍
options: Unchecked human emotions can cause mass destruction 💥
answer: Unchecked human emotions can cause mass destruction 💥
explanation: Perfect! Frost uses nature as a metaphor to warn us that extremes of human emotion—whether passionate desire or cold hatred—will lead to our downfall. 🧠
hint: It talks about the dangers of extreme human feelings.

question: In 'A Letter to God', why did Lencho go out into the rain initially? 🌧️
options: To have the pleasure of feeling the rain on his body 😌
To cover his crops with a tarp 🏕️
answer: To have the pleasure of feeling the rain on his body 😌
explanation: Awesome! He was so happy that the much-needed rain had finally arrived that he went out just to enjoy the feeling of it on his skin. 💧
hint: He wanted to enjoy the sensation of the drops.

question: What did the postmaster do to keep Lencho's faith alive? 🕊️
options: He replied to the letter and sent money ✉️
answer: He replied to the letter and sent money ✉️
explanation: Fantastic! The postmaster acted with deep empathy; he didn't just reply, but actually collected money to help a man he had never met. ❤️
hint: He took practical action by collecting something valuable.

question: How did the poet in 'Dust of Snow' feel before the snow fell on him? 😔
explanation: Spot on! The poet was having a terrible day and was in a depressive, rueful mood until nature intervened and lifted his spirits. ✨
hint: He mentioned that he had 'rued' the day.
